summary.summary:
Migrated copier from pydantic 1 to pydantic 2. Full suite: 691 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped (the skips were already present before the migration).

Changes:
- copier/errors.py: removed the v1-only `pydantic.errors._PathValueError` import. PathNotAbsoluteError and PathNotRelativeError now subclass ValueError and format their own message, so validators still raise ValidationError.
- copier/types.py: replaced the `path_validator`/`__get_validators__` hooks with `AbsolutePath = Annotated[Path, AfterValidator(path_is_absolute)]` and `RelativePath = Annotated[Path, AfterValidator(path_is_relative)]`. Removed the unused AllowArbitraryTypes helper.
- copier/template.py: Task uses `ConfigDict(coerce_numbers_to_str=True)` so numeric items in task command lists (e.g. `[python, "...", 2]`) are still accepted as in v1.
- copier/user_data.py: `@validator` became `@field_validator` (+ `@classmethod`); `always=True` became `Field(default="", validate_default=True)`; `values` became `info.data`. Question uses `ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)`.
- copier/main.py:
  - `Worker` is now a stdlib `dataclass`, so unknown kwargs raise TypeError as the tests require. Its `__post_init__` validates the init arguments through a pydantic model built with `create_model` from the class's type hints (`get_type_hints(..., include_extras=True)`), and writes the validated values back. Wrong values still raise pydantic ValidationError.
  - `Extra.forbid` config removed. `to_json` filter uses `pydantic_core.to_jsonable_python` instead of `pydantic.json.pydantic_encoder`.
- pyproject.toml: pydantic pin changed from `>=1.10.2,<2` to `>=2.5,<3`.

Items for review (not verified here):
- The `>=2.5` floor is my estimate (coerce_numbers_to_str/AfterValidator era); I did not run the suite against 2.5 specifically.
- poetry.lock still pins pydantic 1.10.11 and needs regenerating with `poetry lock`.
- pydantic 1 coerced numbers to str in every str field; only Task has coerce_numbers_to_str. Fields such as Question.help or var_name could reject numeric YAML values. No test covers this.
- Worker's validation now goes through a create_model shadow model instead of a pydantic dataclass, a design choice worth a reviewer's look.
- Python floor (>=3.7) unchanged; newer pydantic 2 releases may need a higher Python.

You can only act through tools:
- list_files, search_code, read_file, edit_file: explore and edit the repository.
- run_tests: run the test suite in a sandbox with pydantic 2 installed. Pass test ids to run a subset; omit them to run everything. Failures are grouped by root cause.
- search_docs: search the official pydantic migration guide. Look up the replacement for an old API before changing it, using exact names from the error or the code.
- finish: call this when every test passes. It triggers a full verification run; if anything still fails you will get the results and must keep working.

Rules:
- Fix the code under test, never the tests. Test files cannot be edited, and tests must not be skipped.
- Do a real migration to the pydantic 2 API. Do not route around it with compatibility shims that keep the old API alive (for Pydantic: no `pydantic.v1` imports).
- Update the dependency pin in the project metadata (pyproject.toml, setup.py/setup.cfg or requirements files) so it allows pydantic 2 and excludes versions the migrated code no longer supports. Also check the pins of companion packages that must move with it (for example web frameworks or plugins built on pydantic): their minimum must support pydantic 2.
- Work one root cause at a time, starting with the largest failure group. Read the code at the reported location before editing it. Prefer small, targeted edits.
- After related edits, re-run the affected tests to check them before moving on.

benefits of Pydantic V2 even when using your own custom types.

`__get_pydantic_json_schema__` functions of a type by annotating it, rather than modifying the type itself.
This provides a powerful and flexible mechanism for integrating third-party types with Pydantic, and in some cases

I've made the migration as far as the test suite allows, but I can't call `finish` yet. One test still fails, and I don't think it can pass with pydantic 2's dataclass semantics without a change to the test or a workaround I don't want to introduce.

## Current status

The last full run reported **696 passed, 2 failed, 5 skipped** (the 2 failures are the same test, `test_flags_extra_fails`). Before the migration, the whole suite failed at import time.

## What I changed

- **`copier/errors.py`**: removed the import of the v1-only `_PathValueError`. `PathNotAbsoluteError` and `PathNotRelativeError` are now `ValueError` subclasses that format their own message. Pydantic v2 turns a `ValueError` raised in a validator into a `ValidationError`, so the behaviour is the same.
- **`copier/types.py`**: removed the `path_validator` and `__get_validators__` hooks. `AbsolutePath` and `RelativePath` are now `Annotated[Path, AfterValidator(...)]`. I also removed the unused `AllowArbitraryTypes` helper.
- **`copier/main.py`**: `Extra.forbid` became `extra="forbid"`. `pydantic.json.pydantic_encoder` was replaced with `pydantic_core.to_jsonable_python` for the `to_json` filter.
- **`copier/user_data.py`**: `@validator` became `@field_validator` with `@classmethod`. `always=True` became `Field(default="", validate_default=True)`, and `values` became `info.data`. The `Question` config is now `ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)`.
- **`copier/template.py`**: `Task` now uses `ConfigDict(coerce_numbers_to_str=True)`. Without it, a command list such as `[python, "...", 2]` fails, because v1 coerced numbers to strings and v2 does not. This fixed `test_migrations_and_tasks`.
- **`pyproject.toml`**: `pydantic = ">=1.10.2,<2"` became `">=2.5,<3"`. Nothing else in the repo pins pydantic. Copier's other dependencies are not pydantic-based, so no companion packages needed changing.

## The remaining failure: `test_flags_extra_fails`

The test expects `copier.Worker(..., i_am_not_a_member=...)` to raise `TypeError`. In pydantic 2.14, `Worker` is a pydantic dataclass with `extra="forbid"`, and an unknown kwarg raises a `ValidationError` instead. The alternative config, `extra="ignore"`, silently drops the kwarg, which is worse. Pydantic doesn't offer a config option that produces `TypeError`.

Getting `TypeError` would mean one of these:
